# Independent audit: supporting cap responses and buffered quantile inverses

Audited in full:
`candidate 8d34ae3d0117f855`.


nonsmooth payment criterion, not the existence of a paying direction.

## 1. Signs and normalizations

For outside support, u/b is the outward unit normal. Relative radial
inward coordinate s has physical normal displacement H_o s. The shifted
cap contains the ray precisely for s<=-tr/(bH_o). Intersecting with the
new endpoint s_t gives gained length (-tr/(bH_o)-s_t)_+, and multiplying
by the radial Jacobian H_o gives (-r/b-v)_+. Its negative sign in the
LOSS formula is correct even for expanding paths.

For inside support the outward normal is -u/b. The cap keeps s>=tr/(bH_o),
so the captured endpoint is max(s_t,tr/(bH_o)). The corresponding loss is
max(v,r/b), equal to v+(r/b-v)_+. Adding all other boundary losses gives
D plus the stated hinge; it does not discard the opposite boundary of an
inside-supported fiber.

The divisor b=||u|| is retained in both formulas. A positive-area supporting
face has the stated unique normal a.e.; its joins do not carry additional
(d-1)-measure. Zero-area supporting faces have zero first contribution.
The d=1 formula uses endpoint counting measure and is exact.

## 2. Uniform first expansion

The assumed uniform O(t) radial displacement provides a uniform O(t) bound
on every affected ray. Outside the old supporting face, only rays in a
shrinking boundary collar can contribute. Their contribution divided by t
is bounded, while their boundary measure tends to zero after removing the
face itself. The inner ball controls the radial Jacobian and denominators.
Bounded a.e. radial speed convergence is L1 by dominated convergence.
The positive-part map is Lipschitz, so the same argument is uniform over
bounded threshold-rate intervals.

On a proper cut, the cutting plane meets the old boundary in surface measure
zero. The proper section area is continuous at its level. The source's
collar argument thus handles simultaneous body and threshold variation;
it does not illegitimately add two derivatives at a supporting jump.

## 3. Inverse continuation

Every hinge term has a nonnegative slope between zero and its facet
coarea. The proper own section supplies a strictly positive common lower
slope, and the finite total section measure supplies the upper slope.
Thus R is increasing, onto, and has a globally Lipschitz inverse.

The exact weighted quantile equation already defines the actual cover.
Its O(t) bracket follows from radial symmetric-difference volume O(t),
alpha(t)=O(t), and the own proper trace's uniformly positive local coarea.
The uniform scalar expansion then applies to all its bounded threshold
rates. Every subsequential loss limit solves the same strictly increasing
weighted inverse equation, so the loss derivative exists without selecting
a generalized derivative or a supporting allocation in advance.

The strict sign is correct: loss ell exceeds beta D iff
sum rho R_j^{-1}(beta D)<alpha'. Equality gives no strict descent.

## 4. Allocations and calibration

The recovered inside allocation multiplies v by 1-sigma; the outside
allocation multiplies v by tau. The same sigma/tau enters its threshold
coarea. Ties give the same scalar response for every allowed selector, so
the harmonic-weight formula is a consequence of the solved shifts, not
an independent optimization variable.

Independent verifier:
`supporting computation verify_supporting_cap_response_audit_defect_transport.py`.
It passes **1,218 exact checks**, using actual perturbed intervals across
all five old statuses, arbitrary signed endpoint speeds, supporting ties,
the explicit piecewise inverse, and two unlike rows sharing one continued
loss. These checks supplement the general radial proof; they do not replace
its higher-dimensional uniformity argument.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
